title: 2024 年全国硕士研究生招生考试 英语（二）

sections.title: Section I　完形填空
sections.dir: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D on ANSWER SHEET 1. (10 points)
sections.note: 主线：社交要讲“平衡”，太少孤独、太多倦怠。6 题举例、10 题 at first 最易丢分。

paras.en: Your social life is defined as the activities you do with other people for pleasure, when you are not working. It's important to have a social life, but what's right for one person won't be right for another. Some of us feel energised by spending lots of time with others, 1, some of us may feel drained, even if it's doing something we enjoy.
paras.zh: 社交生活指的是你在不工作时与他人一起为了消遣而做的活动。拥有社交生活很重要，但适合一个人的方式未必适合另一个人。我们中有些人因为与他人共度大量时间而精力充沛，1，另一些人却可能感到精疲力竭，即便做的正是自己喜欢的事。

paras.en: This is why finding a 2 in your social life is key. Spending too much time on your own, not 3 others, can make you feel lonely and 4. Loneliness is known to impact on your mental health and 5 a low mood. Anyone can feel lonely at any time. This might be especially true if, 6, you are working from home and you are 7 on the usual social conversations that happen in an office. Other life changes can 8 periods of loneliness too, such as retirement, changing jobs or becoming a parent.
paras.zh: 正因如此，在社交生活中找到 2 才是关键。独处时间过长、不去 3 他人，会让你感到孤独和 4。众所周知，孤独会影响心理健康，并 5 情绪低落。任何人都可能在任何时候感到孤独。如果 6 你正在居家办公，7 了办公室里日常的闲聊，这种情况可能尤其明显。其他人生变化同样会 8 一段时期的孤独，比如退休、换工作或初为父母。

paras.en: It's important to recognise these feelings of loneliness. There are ways to 9 a social life, but it can feel overwhelming 10. It's a great idea to start by thinking about hobbies you enjoy. You can then find groups and activities related to those where you will be able to meet 11 people. There are groups aimed at new parents, at those who want to 12 a new sport for the first time, or networking events for those in the same profession to meet up and 13 ideas.
paras.zh: 识别出这些孤独感很重要。有办法可以 9 社交生活，但 10 可能会让人觉得不堪重负。一个很好的起点是先想想你喜欢的爱好。然后你可以找到与这些爱好相关的群体和活动，在那里你能遇到 11 的人。有些群体面向新手父母，有些面向想第一次 12 一项新运动的人，还有一些社交活动让同行相聚、13 想法。

paras.en: On the other hand, it's 14 possible to have too much of a social life. If you feel like you're always doing something and there is never any 15 in your calendar for downtime, you could suffer social burnout or social 16. We all have our own social limit and it's important to recognise when you're feeling like it's all too much. Low mood, low energy, irritability and trouble sleeping could all be 17 of poor social health. Make sure you 18 some time in your diary when you're 19 for socialising and use this time to relax, 20 and recover.
paras.zh: 另一方面，社交生活过多也是 14 可能的。如果你觉得自己总在忙事情，日程表里从来没有 15 留给休息，你可能会社交倦怠，或者出现社交 16。每个人都有自己的社交上限，重要的是在感觉“实在太多”时能够察觉。情绪低落、精力不足、易怒和睡眠不佳，都可能是社交健康不良的 17。一定要在日程本里 18 出一段时间，19 安排社交，用这段时间放松、20 和恢复。

items.exp: 定位首段 Some of us feel energised..., some of us may feel drained：前句“精力充沛”，后句“精疲力竭”，前后相反，需要对比连词，故 whereas。because 表因果，会把两种相反感受说成同一原因；unless 表条件、until 表时间，都无法连接这两个并列分句，且与逗号后的逗号结构不合。
定位第二段首句 finding a ___ in your social life is key。下文一讲独处太久会孤独（3、4 题），一讲社交过多会倦怠（14 题以后），两端都要防，故 balance（平衡）。contrast 只表示“对比”，不含“适度”之意；gap（缺口）与 link（联系）都概括不了“不多不少”。
定位 Spending too much time on your own, not ___ others。on your own 与 not ___ others 是同一意思的正反复现：“独处”即“不见别人”，故 seeing。pleasing（取悦）、judging（评判）把一个中性动作写成讨好或评价；teaching（教导）更是给句子加了原文没有的角色。
定位 can make you feel lonely and ___。and 并列两个同向后果，lonely 之外应是“与外界脱节”，故 disconnected。misguided（被误导的）、spoiled（被宠坏的）都带道德评价，与“独处”无必然联系；surprised 只是一时情绪，无法与 lonely 构成递进。
定位 Loneliness is known to impact on your mental health and ___ a low mood。and 连接两个同向谓语：孤独既“影响心理健康”，也“导致情绪低落”，故 contribute to（促成）。rely on（依赖）、go against（违背）方向相反；interfere with 若代入便成“干扰低落情绪”，语义颠倒。
定位 This might be especially true if, ___, you are working from home。上句是“任何人随时都可能孤独”的总说，本句举居家办公为具体场合，是总—分关系，故 for example。in fact 表递进强调，of course 表理所当然，on average 表统计平均，三者都引不出例证。

定位 you are working from home and you are ___ on the usual social conversations that happen in an office。居家办公自然“错过”办公室的日常闲聊，miss out on 为固定搭配，故 B。cut back on 指“削减”用量，与闲聊不搭；break in 表“打断、闯入”，look down on 表“看不起”，语义都偏。
定位 Other life changes can ___ periods of loneliness too, such as retirement。退休、换工作、初为父母都是“引发”孤独的诱因，故 trigger。shorten（缩短）与“出现孤独”方向相反；follow（跟随）把因果主客颠倒；interrupt（打断）需要有一个正在进行的过程作宾语。
定位 There are ways to ___ a social life, but it can feel overwhelming at first。上文说孤独会侵蚀社交，此处指把社交“重新建立起来”，故 regain（重新获得）。assess（评估）、interpret（解读）只停在认识层面，不动手做事；provide 与 a social life 搭配生硬，且不含“失而复得”之意。
定位 There are ways to regain a social life, but it can feel overwhelming ___。but 表转折：办法虽有，起步那阵子却让人不知所措，故 at first（起初）。in turn 表因果链上的“反过来”，on time 表准时，by chance 表偶然，都与“难在开头”这层时间意义不合。

定位 find groups and activities related to those where you will be able to meet ___ people。按自己的爱好找社群，遇到的自然是兴趣相同的人，故 like-minded（志同道合的）。far-sighted（有远见）、strong-willed（意志坚定）、kind-hearted（善良）都是对品性的评价，与“同好”无关。
定位 those who want to ___ a new sport for the first time。for the first time 已点明“初次”，与 try（尝试）呼应，故 A。promote（推广）主语会是组织者而非参与者；watch（观看）与“第一次做一项运动”的参与义不符；describe（描述）更与运动实践无关。
定位 networking events for those in the same profession to meet up and ___ ideas。同行聚会除了见面，就是“交流”想法，故 share。test（检验）、revise（修改）都预设想法有问题，accept（接受）只单向接收，体现不出 networking 的互通有无。
定位 On the other hand, it's ___ possible to have too much of a social life。上文讲社交太少之弊，此处转到另一极端，是“同样”会出问题，故 also。thus 表因果，但 on the other hand 是并列转折而非因果；already 表已然，only 表限定，都接不上“另一面”。
定位 there is never any ___ in your calendar for downtime。日程表里缺的是“空档、留白”，故 space。list（清单）与 order（顺序）说的是排列方式，boundary（边界）指界限，都不能表达“没有余暇时间”这一意思。
定位 you could suffer social burnout or social ___。or 连接两个近义项，burnout（倦怠）对应的身心状态是 fatigue（疲劳），故 A。criticism（批评）、injustice（不公）是外界加诸的评价，dilemma（两难）是一种处境，都不是“社交过量”导致的身体反应。
定位 Low mood, low energy, irritability and trouble sleeping could all be ___ of poor social health。所列四项都是症状，是社交健康不良的“信号”，故 signs。sources 会把症状说成病因，因果颠倒；standards（标准）与 scores（分数）跟症状描述完全不在一个语义场。
定位 Make sure you ___ some time in your diary。在日程本里“划出、留出”一段时间，故 mark out。take over（接管）对象是职责，wipe off（擦掉）是清除已有内容，add up（合计）是数字累加，三者都不能与 some time in your diary 搭配出“预留”之意。
定位 when you're ___ for socialising and use this time to relax。这段时间是要“不安排社交”的，故 unavailable for（无暇、不接待）。ungrateful（忘恩负义）、regretful（后悔）都是情绪形容词；responsible for 意为“对……负责”，与“留白休息”正相反。
定位 use this time to relax, ___ and recover。三个动词同向递进：放松、休息、恢复，故 rest。react（反应）与 repeat（重复）都无法与 recover 构成这种递进；return（返回）缺“返回何处”的宾语，句子不完整。

sections.title: Text 1　数字经济的分配难题
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主题：数字红利分配不均，AI 又集中在大城市。25 题落在末段“重新定义 AI 角色”。

paras.en: In her new book Cogs and Monsters: What Economics Is, and What It Should Be, Diane Coyle, an economist at Cambridge University, argues that the digital economy requires new ways of thinking about progress. “Whatever we mean by the economy growing, by things getting better, the gains will have to be more evenly shared than in the recent past,” she writes. “An economy of tech millionaires or billionaires and gig workers, with middle-income jobs undercut by automation, will not be politically sustainable.”
paras.zh: 剑桥大学经济学家黛安·科伊尔在新书《齿轮与怪物：经济学是什么，以及它应该是什么》中提出，数字经济需要关于“进步”的新思路。她写道：“无论我们所说的经济增长、事情变好指的是什么，收益都必须比过去更平均地分享。”“一个由科技百万富翁或亿万富翁与零工劳动者构成、中等收入岗位被自动化削低的经济体，在政治上是不可持续的。”

paras.en: Improving living standards and increasing prosperity for more people will require greater use of digital technologies to boost productivity in various sectors, including health care and construction, says Coyle. But people can't be expected to embrace the changes if they're not seeing the benefits - if they're just seeing good jobs being destroyed.
paras.zh: 科伊尔说，要提高更多人的生活水平、让更多人富裕起来，就需要在包括医疗和建筑在内的各个部门更多地使用数字技术以提高生产率。但如果人们看不到好处——只看到好工作被毁掉——就不能指望他们拥抱这些变化。

paras.en: In a recent interview, Coyle said she fears that tech's inequality problem could be a roadblock to deploying AI. “We're talking about disruption,” she says. “These are transformative technologies that change the ways we spend our time every day, that change business models that succeed.” To make such “tremendous changes,” she adds, you need social buy-in.
paras.zh: 在最近一次采访中，科伊尔说，她担心科技行业的不平等问题会成为部署人工智能的障碍。“我们谈的是颠覆，”她说，“这些是变革性技术，会改变我们每天安排时间的方式，也会改变成功的商业模式。”她补充说，要促成这样的“巨大变化”，你需要社会的认可。

paras.en: Instead, says Coyle, resentment is simmering among many as the benefits are perceived to go to elites in a handful of prosperous cities.
paras.zh: 科伊尔说，事实恰恰相反：由于人们认为好处都流向了少数繁荣城市里的精英，许多人心中正积攒着不满。

paras.en: According to the Brookings Institution, a short list of eight American cities that included San Francisco, San Jose, Boston, and Seattle had roughly 38% of all tech jobs by 2019. New AI technologies are particularly concentrated: Brookings's Mark Muro and Sifan Liu estimate that just 15 cities account for two-thirds of the AI assets and capabilities in the United States.
paras.zh: 布鲁金斯学会的数据显示，截至 2019 年，包括旧金山、圣何塞、波士顿和西雅图在内的八座美国城市拥有全国约 38% 的科技岗位。新的人工智能技术尤其集中：布鲁金斯学会的马克·穆罗和西凡·刘估计，仅 15 座城市就占了全美三分之二的人工智能资产与能力。

paras.en: The dominance of a few cities in the invention and commercialization of AI means that geographical disparities in wealth will continue to soar. Not only will this foster political and social unrest, but it could, as Coyle suggests, hold back the sorts of AI technologies needed for regional economies to grow.
paras.zh: 少数城市在人工智能的发明与商业化中占据主导，意味着财富的地域差距将继续拉大。这不仅会助长政治与社会动荡，而且正如科伊尔所言，还可能阻碍区域经济增长所需的那类人工智能技术。

paras.en: Part of the solution could lie in somehow loosening the strangle hold that Big Tech has on defining the AI agenda. That will likely take increased federal funding for research independent of the tech giants.
paras.zh: 部分解决办法可能在于设法松动大科技公司对“人工智能议程”定义权的把持。这很可能需要增加联邦资助，用于独立于科技巨头的研究。

paras.en: A more immediate response is to broaden our digital imaginations to conceive of AI technologies that don't simply replace jobs but expand opportunities in the sectors that different parts of the country care most about, like health care, education, and manufacturing.
paras.zh: 更直接的做法是拓宽我们的数字想象力，去设想那样的人工智能技术：它不只是取代岗位，而是在全国各地最关心的领域——如医疗、教育和制造业——扩大机会。

items.stem: Coyle argues in her new book that economic growth should
items.exp: 定位第一段引文：the gains will have to be more evenly shared than in the recent past——增长的收益要“更平均地分享”，即让民众平等受益，故 C。A 把 innovations 当成目的，原文的技术只是手段；D 的“强力推动增长”是速度问题，而科伊尔谈的是分配，方向错位。

items.stem: According to Paragraph 2, digital technologies should be used to
items.exp: 定位第二段首句：greater use of digital technologies to boost productivity in various sectors——用数字技术提升各部门生产率，即提高整体工作效率，故 C。D 借 various sectors 设套，但原文说的是“各部门都提效”，不是跨部门协作；A 的 instant 与提升生产率的渐进过程不符；B 的“减轻工作量”原文未提。

items.stem: What does Coyle fear about transformative technologies?
opts: They may be impractical to deploy
They may be unwelcome to the public
items.exp: 定位第三段：she fears that tech's inequality problem could be a roadblock to deploying AI，紧接着强调 To make such “tremendous changes”... you need social buy-in——她怕的是公众不买账，故 D。B 把 roadblock 读成“技术上行不通”，其实阻碍来自社会态度；A 的“工作与生活平衡”由 change the ways we spend our time 改装而来，属偷换。

items.stem: Several American cities are mentioned to show
opts: the uneven distribution of AI technologies in the US
the disappointing prospect of tech jobs in the US
the increasing significance of US AI assets
items.exp: 定位第五、六段：八座城市占 38% 科技岗位、15 座城市占三分之二 AI 资产，随后一句收束为 geographical disparities in wealth will continue to soar——举例是为了说明分布不均，故 A。B 把“岗位集中”读成“前景黯淡”；C 与 hold back regional economies 相反；D 谈“AI 资产更重要”，原文谈的是“更集中”。

items.stem: With regard to Coyle's concern, the author suggests
opts: raising funds to start new AI projects
guarding against the side effects of AI
redefining the role of AI technologies
items.exp: 定位末段：broaden our digital imaginations to conceive of AI technologies that don't simply replace jobs but expand opportunities——作者主张把 AI 从“替代岗位”重新定位为“扩大机会”，故 D。A 借上段 increased federal funding 设套，但原文资助的是“独立于巨头的研究”，不是“启动新项目”；B 的 collaboration 文中无据。

sections.title: Text 2　英国的木材缺口
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主题：不种树就没木材，建筑业将受冲击。27 题“力度不够”不是“时机不对”。

paras.en: The UK is facing a future construction crisis because of a failure to plant trees to produce wood, Confor has warned. The forestry and wood trade body has called for urgent action to reduce the country's reliance on timber imports and provide a stable supply of wood for future generations. Currently only 20 percent of the UK's wood requirement is home-grown while it remains the second-largest net importer of timber in the world.
paras.zh: 林业与木材行业组织 Confor 警告说，由于未能种树产木材，英国将面临未来的建筑危机。该组织呼吁采取紧急行动，减少英国对进口木材的依赖，并为子孙后代提供稳定的木材供应。目前英国木材需求中只有 20% 来自本国，而它仍是世界第二大木材净进口国。

paras.en: Coming at a time of fresh incentives from the UK government for landowners to grow more trees, the trade body says these don't go far enough and fail to promote the benefits of planting them to boost timber supplies. “Not only are we facing a carbon crisis now, but we will also be facing a future construction crisis because of failure to plant trees to produce wood,” said Stuart Goodall, chief executive of Confor. “For decades we have not taken responsibility for investing in our domestic wood supply, leaving us exposed to fluctuating prices and fighting for future supplies of wood as global demand rises and our own supplies fall.”
paras.zh: 这些表态恰逢英国政府出台新激励措施、鼓励地主多种树，而该行业组织表示，这些措施力度不够，也未能宣传种树对增加木材供应的好处。“我们现在不仅面临碳危机，还将因为没能种树产木材而面临未来的建筑危机，”Confor 首席执行官斯图尔特·古德尔说。“几十年来，我们一直没有承担起投资本国木材供应的责任，这使我们暴露在价格波动之中，并随着全球需求上升、本国供应下降，为未来的木材供应苦苦争夺。”

paras.en: The UK has ideal conditions for growing wood to build low-carbon homes and is a global leader in certifying that its forests are sustainably managed, Confor says. While around three quarters of Scottish homes are built from Scottish timber, the use of home-grown wood in England is only around 25 percent.
paras.zh: Confor 说，英国拥有种植木材、建造低碳住宅的理想条件，在认证森林可持续经营方面也是全球领先者。苏格兰约四分之三的住宅用苏格兰木材建造，而英格兰使用本国木材的比例仅约 25%。

paras.en: While productive tree planting can deliver real financial benefits to rural economies and contribute to the UK's net-zero strategy, the focus of government support continues to be on food production and the rewilding and planting of native woodland solely for biodiversity. Goodall adds: “While food production and biodiversity are clearly of critical importance, we need our land to also provide secure supplies of wood for construction, manufacturing and contribute to net zero.”
paras.zh: 虽然生产性造林能给乡村经济带来实实在在的经济收益，并有助于英国实现净零战略，但政府支持的重点仍放在粮食生产，以及纯粹为生物多样性而修复和种植原生林地。古德尔补充说：“粮食生产和生物多样性显然至关重要，但我们也需要土地为建筑、制造业提供可靠的木材供应，并为净零作出贡献。”

paras.en: “While the UK government has stated its ambition for more tree planting, there has been little action on the ground.” Confor is now calling for much greater impetus behind those aspirations to ensure we have enough wood to meet increasing demand.
paras.zh: “虽然英国政府已表态要种更多树，但实际情况是几乎没有行动。”Confor 现在呼吁为这些愿景注入大得多的推动力，以确保我们有足够的木材满足日益增长的需求。

items.stem: It can be learned from paragraph 1 that the UK needs to
opts: lift its control on timber import
items.exp: 定位第一段：only 20 percent of the UK's wood requirement is home-grown，该组织又呼吁 reduce reliance on timber imports and provide a stable supply of wood——自给率太低，要扩大本国木材供应，故 A。B 的“减少木材需求”与 provide a stable supply 矛盾，要的是供给而非压需求；D 的“放松进口管制”方向也反，文中要减少对进口的依赖。

items.stem: According to Confor, the UK government's fresh incentives
opts: can hardly address a construction crisis
are believed to come at a wrong time
seem to be misleading for landowners
will be too costly to put into practice
items.exp: 定位第二段：these don't go far enough and fail to promote the benefits of planting them to boost timber supplies——“力度不够、没起到鼓励作用”，自然难以化解建筑用材危机，故 A。B 把 coming at a time of fresh incentives（新激励出台之际）这一时间状语读成“时机不对”；C 的 misleading 指“误导地主”，原文只说激励不足、宣传不到位。

items.stem: The UK's exposure to fluctuating wood prices is a result of
opts: the government's inaction on timber imports
the competition among timber traders at home
Wood producers' motive to maximise profits
items.exp: 定位第二段末引语：For decades we have not taken responsibility for investing in our domestic wood supply, leaving us exposed to fluctuating prices——价格受制于人是“长期不投资本国木材供应”的结果，故 B。A 把“不投资造林”换成“对进口不作为”，偷换了对象；D 谈生产商逐利，而原文归因于行业与政府未投资。

items.stem: Which of the following causes the shortage of wood supply in the UK?
opts: Outdated technologies of the wood industry
items.exp: 定位第四段：the focus of government support continues to be on food production and the rewilding and planting of native woodland solely for biodiversity——政策只鼓励种粮与生态林，地主自然不愿营造用材林，故 D。B 与第三段 has ideal conditions 正相反；A 的“消费过量”与 C 的“技术落后”文中都没有依据。

items.stem: What does Goodall think the UK government should do?
opts: Subsidise the building of low-carbon homes
Pay greater attention to boosting rural economies
Provide more support for productive tree planting
Give priority to pursuing its net-zero strategy
items.exp: 定位末段：Confor is now calling for much greater impetus behind those aspirations——要求给“多种树”的愿景更大推力，即更多支持生产性造林，故 C。B 的“振兴乡村经济”是造林的附带好处，不是古德尔的诉求；D 把 net-zero 这一背景当成优先事项；A 的“补贴低碳住宅”文中未提。

sections.title: Text 3　高龄驾驶者的去留
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主题：让高龄司机停驶难在各管一段。33 题 piecemeal 是“零敲碎打”，对应需协调。

paras.en: One big challenge in keeping unsafe aging drivers off the road is convincing them that it is time to turn over the key. It is a complete life-changer when someone stops—or is forced to stop—driving, said former risk manager Anne M. Menke.
paras.zh: 要让不安全的高龄驾驶者远离道路，一大挑战是说服他们该交出车钥匙了。前风险经理安妮·M. 门克说，当一个人停止开车——或被迫停止开车——生活会发生彻底的改变。

paras.en: The American Medical Association advises physicians that in situation where clear evidence of substantial driving impairment implies a strong threat to patient and public safety, and where the physician's advice to discontinue driving privileges is ignored, it is desirable and ethical to notify the Department of Motor Vehicles, Menke wrote. “Some states require physicians to report, others allow but do not mandate reports, while a few consider a report breach of confidentiality. There could be liability and penalties if a physician does not act in accordance with state laws on reporting and confidentiality,” she counseled.
paras.zh: 门克写道，美国医学会建议医生：在有明确证据表明驾驶能力受到实质性损害、对患者和公共安全构成强烈威胁，且医生停止其驾驶资格的建议被忽视的情况下，通知机动车管理局是可取且合乎伦理的。“有些州要求医生上报，有些州允许但不强制上报，还有少数州认为上报即违反保密义务。如果医生未按各州关于上报与保密的法律行事，可能面临责任与处罚，”她提醒说。

paras.en: Part of the problem in keeping older drivers safe is that the difficulties are addressed piecemeal by different professions with different focuses, including gerontologists, highway administration officials, automotive engineers and others, said gerontologist Elizabeth Dugan. “There's not a National Institute of Older Driver Studies,” she said. “We need better evidence on what makes drivers unsafe” and what can help, said Dugan.
paras.zh: 老年病学家伊丽莎白·杜根说，维护老年驾驶者安全的部分问题在于，这些难题由不同专业各自零散地处理，关注点各不相同，涉及老年病学家、公路管理部门官员、汽车工程师等。“并没有一所‘全国老年驾驶者研究所’，”她说。杜根说：“我们需要更好的证据，弄清是什么让驾驶者变得不安全”，以及什么办法有帮助。

paras.en: One thing that does seem to work is requiring drivers to report in person for license renewal. Mandatory in-person renewal was associated with a 31 percent reduction in fatal crashes involving drivers 85 or older, according to one study. Passing vision tests also produced a similar decline in fatal crashes for those drivers, although there appeared to be no benefit from combining the two.
paras.zh: 似乎确实有效的一点，是要求驾驶者本人到场换证。一项研究显示，强制本人到场换证与 85 岁及以上驾驶者致命事故减少 31% 相关。通过视力测试也使这些驾驶者的致命事故出现类似下降，不过两者结合似乎并没有额外好处。

paras.en: Many old drivers don't see eye doctors or can't afford to. Primary care providers have their hands full and may not be able to follow through with patients who have trouble driving because they can't turn their heads or remember where they are going—or have gotten shorter and haven't changed their seat settings sufficiently to reach car pedals easily.
paras.zh: 许多老年驾驶者不看眼科医生，或者负担不起。基层医生已经忙不过来，可能无法跟进那些开车有困难的患者——他们转不了头，或者记不住自己要去哪里；也可能是个子变矮了，却没有充分调整座椅，难以轻松够到踏板。

paras.en: As long as there are other cars on the roads, self-driving cars won't solve the problems of crashes, said Dugan. Avoiding dangers posed by all those human drivers would require too many algorithms, she said. But we need to do more to improve safety, said Dugan. “If we're going to have 100-year lives, we need cars that a 90-year-old can drive comfortably.”
paras.zh: 杜根说，只要路上还有其他车，自动驾驶汽车就解决不了碰撞问题。她说，要避开所有这些人类驾驶者带来的危险，需要太多算法。但杜根说，我们还需要做更多来提升安全。“如果我们要活到 100 岁，就需要 90 岁的人也能舒适驾驶的汽车。”

items.stem: According to paragraph 1, keeping unsafe aging drivers off the road
opts: can be a tough task to complete
will be beneficial to their health
items.exp: 定位第一段首句：One big challenge ... is convincing them that it is time to turn over the key——难在“说服”，是一项很难完成的任务，故 C。B 的 disputed 指“有争议”，文中说的是执行之难，不是意见分歧；A 的“新安全措施”与 D 的“有益健康”在首段都找不到依据。

items.stem: The American Medical Association's advice
items.exp: 定位第二段引语：Some states require physicians to report, others allow but do not mandate reports, while a few consider a report breach of confidentiality——有的州强制、有的州允许、少数州视为泄密，各州反应不一，故 D。A 的“赢得司机支持”文中未提；C 的 widely dismissed 过于绝对，忽略了“要求上报”的那一类州。

items.stem: According to Dugan, efforts to keep older drivers safe
items.exp: 定位第三段：the difficulties are addressed piecemeal by different professions with different focuses——“零敲碎打、各管一段”正是问题所在，言下之意是需要统筹协调，故 B。A 与“没有全国性研究所”的现状相反；D 的“法律支持”属第二段医生上报的话题，不是杜根的判断。

items.stem: Some older drivers have trouble driving because they tend to
items.exp: 定位第五段：patients who have trouble driving because they can't turn their heads or remember where they are going——记不住要去哪里，即记忆力衰退，故 B。C 把 can't turn their heads（脖子转不动）误读成慢性疼痛；A 的“坏习惯”与 D 的“不保养车”文中均无，属常识补足。

items.stem: Dugan thinks that the solution to the problems of crashes may lie
opts: adjusting the age limit for drivers
items.exp: 定位末段引语：we need cars that a 90-year-old can drive comfortably——需要适合高龄者驾驶的汽车，故 B。A 与 self-driving cars won't solve the problems 直接冲突，是最强干扰；C 的“改造交通设施”与 D 的“调整年龄上限”文中均未提及。

sections.title: Text 4　健康类应用与隐私
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主题：健康 App 的数据落在法律缝隙里。37 题问“暗示”，落在保护范围要扩。

paras.en: If you look at the apps on your phone, chances are you have at least one related to your health — and probably several. Whether it is a mental health app, a fitness tracker, a connected health device or something else, many of us are taking advantage of this technology to keep better track of our health in some shape or form. Recent research from the Organization for the Review of Care and Health Applications found that 350,000 health apps were available on the market, 90,000 of which launched in 2020 alone.
paras.zh: 看看你手机上的应用，你很可能至少有一个与健康有关——而且可能有好几个。无论是心理健康应用、健身追踪器、联网健康设备还是别的什么，我们中许多人都在以某种形式利用这类技术更好地追踪自己的健康。健康护理应用评估组织近期的研究发现，市场上有 35 万个健康类应用，其中 9 万个是 2020 年一年内上线的。

paras.en: While these apps have a great deal to offer, it is not always clear how the personal information we input is collected, safeguarded and shared online. Existing health privacy law, such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, is primarily focused on the way hospitals, doctors' offices, clinics and insurance companies store health records online. The health information these apps and health data tracking wearables are collecting typically does not receive the same legal protections.
paras.zh: 这些应用固然能提供很多，但我们输入的个人信息在网上如何被收集、保护和共享，却并不总是清楚。现行健康隐私法，如《健康保险携带与责任法案》，主要针对医院、医生诊所、门诊部和保险公司在网上存储健康记录的方式。而这些应用和健康数据追踪可穿戴设备所收集的健康信息，通常得不到同样的法律保护。

paras.en: Without additional protections in place, companies may share (and potentially monetize) personal health information in a way consumers may not have authorized or anticipated. In 2021, Flo Health faced a Federal Trade Commission (FTC) investigation. The FTC alleged in a complaint that “despite express privacy claims, the company took control of users' sensitive fertility data and shared it with third parties.” Flo Health and the FTC settled the matter with a Consent Order requiring the company to get app users' express affirmative consent before sharing their health information as well as to instruct the third parties to delete the data they had obtained.
paras.zh: 在没有额外保护的情况下，企业可能以消费者未曾授权或预料的方式共享（并可能借以牟利）个人健康信息。2021 年，Flo Health 公司遭到联邦贸易委员会（FTC）调查。FTC 在一份投诉中称，“尽管明确作出隐私承诺，该公司仍掌控了用户的敏感生育数据，并与第三方共享”。Flo Health 与 FTC 以一份同意令了结此事，要求该公司在共享用户健康信息前取得用户的明确肯定同意，并指示第三方删除其已获取的数据。

paras.en: Section 5 of the FTC Act empowers the FTC to initiate enforcement action against unfair or deceptive acts, meaning the FTC can only act after the fact if a company's privacy practices are misleading or cause unjustified consumer harm. While the FTC is doing what it can to ensure apps are keeping their promises to consumers around the handling of their sensitive health information, the rate at which these health apps are hitting the market demonstrates just how immense of a challenge this is.
paras.zh: 《联邦贸易委员会法》第 5 条授权 FTC 对不公平或欺骗性行为采取执法行动，这意味着只有当企业的隐私做法具有误导性、或造成不合理的消费者损害时，FTC 才能事后介入。尽管 FTC 正在尽力确保应用在敏感健康信息的处理上兑现对消费者的承诺，但这些健康应用进入市场的速度表明，这一挑战有多么巨大。

paras.en: As to the prospects for federal legislation, commentators suggest that comprehensive federal privacy legislation seems unlikely in the short term. States have begun implementing their own solutions to shore up protections for consumer-generated health data. California has been at the forefront of state privacy efforts with the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018. Virginia, Colorado and Utah have also recently passed state consumer data privacy legislation.
paras.zh: 至于联邦立法的前景，评论人士认为，短期内不太可能出台全面的联邦隐私立法。各州已开始实施自己的方案，以加强对消费者生成健康数据的保护。加州凭借 2018 年《加州消费者隐私法》一直走在州级隐私保护的前列。弗吉尼亚、科罗拉多和犹他等州最近也通过了本州的消费者数据隐私立法。

items.stem: The research findings are cited in paragraph 1 to show
items.exp: 定位第一段末：350,000 health apps were available on the market, 90,000 of which launched in 2020 alone——引数据是为了说明健康类应用数量之多、之普遍，故 A。C 把 smartphone 当主角，原文主语始终是 health apps；B 的“公众健康担忧”与这组数字无关，D 的“技术进步”也非引数据的目的。

items.stem: What does the author imply about existing health privacy law?
opts: Its coverage needs to be extended
items.exp: 定位第二段：现行法 is primarily focused on the way hospitals, doctors' offices, clinics and insurance companies store health records，而 App 与可穿戴设备收集的信息 does not receive the same legal protections——言下之意是保护范围要延伸到 App，故 A。B 的“执法力度”是第四段 FTC 的话题；C 把“未覆盖”读成“已见效”，D 的“保险公司失望”文中无据。

items.stem: Before sharing its users' health information, Flo Health is required to
opts: Seek the approval of the FTC
items.exp: 定位第三段末：requiring the company to get app users' express affirmative consent before sharing their health information——须先取得用户明确的肯定同意，故 D。A 把 FTC 这个监管者当成审批方，同意令并未要求逐次报批；C 张冠李戴，“删除数据”的要求是针对已获取数据的第三方。

items.stem: What challenge is the FTC currently faced with?
opts: The rapid increase in new health apps
The subtle deceptiveness of health apps
The difficulty in assessing consumer harm
items.exp: 定位第四段末：the rate at which these health apps are hitting the market demonstrates just how immense of a challenge this is——挑战来自应用上市的速度，故 B。C 的“隐蔽欺骗性”与 D 的“损害难评估”都出自同一段对 Section 5 适用条件的说明，是执法门槛而非 FTC 面临的主要难题；A 的“信息复杂”文中未提。

items.stem: It can be learned from the last paragraph that health data protection
opts: has been embrace by health app developers
has been a focus of federal policy-making
has gained legislative support in some states
items.exp: 定位末段：Virginia, Colorado and Utah have also recently passed state consumer data privacy legislation——多个州已立法，故 D。B 与 comprehensive federal privacy legislation seems unlikely in the short term 相反；C 把加州“走在前列”读成“遭遇反对”；A 的“开发者拥护”文中没有任何依据。

sections.title: Section II Part B　多项对应（人名观点匹配）
sections.dir: Read the following text and match each of the numbered items in the left column to its corresponding information in the right column. There are two extra choices in the right column. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
sections.note: 五个人名对应五条主张。D、F 分别出自 Valdes 与 Adegboyega-Edun，二人不在题号内。
subs: Students who stand out in a specific extracurricular activity will be favored by top-tier institutions.
Students whose extracurricular activity has benefited their community are likely to win a scholarship.
Undertaking too many extracurricular activities will hardly be seen as a plus by colleges.
A student who exhibits abilities in doing business can impress colleges.
High school students participating in popular activity should excel in it.
Engaging in uncommon activities can demonstrate students' determination and dedication.
It is advisable for students to choose an extracurricular activity that is related to their future study at college.
sections.intro:
High school students eager to stand out in the college application process often participate in a litany of extracurricular activities hoping to bolster their chances of admission a selective undergraduate institution.

However, college admissions experts say that the quality of a college hopeful's extracurricular activities matter more than the number of activities he or she participates in.

blocks.en: Sue Rexford, the director of college guidance at the Charles E. Smith Jewish Day School, says it is not necessary for a student, filling out the Common Application, to list 10 activities in the application. “No college will expect that a student has a huge laundry list of extracurricular that they have been passionately involved in each for an extended period of time,” Rexford wrote in an email.
blocks.zh: 查尔斯·E. 史密斯犹太走读学校升学指导主任苏·雷克斯福德说，学生在填写“通用申请表”时，没有必要在申请表里列出 10 项活动。雷克斯福德在邮件中写道：“没有哪所大学会指望学生有一长串课外活动，而且每一项都充满热情地投入了很长时间。”
blocks.exp: 定位第三、四段：Rexford 说 list 10 activities 并非必要，No college will expect that a student has a huge laundry list——列的太多不会被当成加分项，故 C。E 的“参加热门活动要做到最好”出自 42 块 Harberson，是本题最强干扰，只看“活动数量”一词就会误配。

blocks.en: Experts say it is tougher to distinguish oneself in a school-affiliated extracurricular activity that is common among high school students than it is to stand out while doing an uncommon activity. “The competition to stand out and make an impact is going to be much stiffer, and so if they're going to do a popular activity, I'd say, be the best at it,” says Sara Harberson, a college admission consultant.
blocks.zh: 专家说，在高中生普遍参加的校内课外活动中脱颖而出，比在做一项不常见活动时出彩更难。“要脱颖而出、产生影响，竞争会激烈得多，所以如果他们要做一项热门活动，我会说，就做到最好，”大学招生顾问萨拉·哈伯森说。
blocks.exp: 定位本块末引语：if they're going to do a popular activity, I'd say, be the best at it——做热门活动就要做到最好，故 E。F 的“不寻常活动体现决心与投入”出自下一块的 Adegboyega-Edun（不在题号内），属于拿文中的同类声音冒充 42 号人物，是本块最隐蔽的干扰。

blocks.en: High school students who have an impressive personal project they are working on independently often impress colleges, experts say. “For example, a student with an interest in entrepreneurship could demonstrate skills and potential by starting a profitable small business,” Olivia Valdes, the founder of Zen Admissions consulting firm, wrote in an email. Joseph Adegboyega-Edun, a Maryland high school guidance counselor, says unconventional extracurricular activities can help students impress college admissions offices, assuming they demonstrated serious commitment. “Again, since one of the big questions high school seniors must consider is ‘What makes you unique?’ having an uncommon extracurricular activity, a conventional one is an advantage,” he wrote in an email. Experts say demonstrating talent in at least one extracurricular activity can help in the college admissions process, especially at top-tier undergraduate institutions. “Distinguishing yourself in one focused type of extracurricular activity can be a positive in the admissions process, especially for highly selective institutions, where having top grades and test scores is not enough,” Katie Kelley, admissions counselor at Ivy Wise admissions consultancy, wrote in an email. “Students need to have that quality or hook that will appeal to admissions officers and allow them to visualize how the student might come and enrich their campus community.”
blocks.zh: 专家说，有令人印象深刻的独立个人项目的高中生，往往能给大学留下好印象。“例如，对创业感兴趣的学生可以通过创办一家盈利的小企业来展示技能和潜力，”Zen Admissions 咨询公司创始人奥利维娅·瓦尔德斯在邮件中写道。马里兰州高中升学顾问约瑟夫·阿德博耶加-埃敦说，非常规的课外活动有助于学生给大学招生办留下印象，前提是他们表现出认真的投入。他在邮件中写道：“而且，既然高中生必须考虑的大问题之一是‘什么让你与众不同’，那么拥有一项不寻常的课外活动，相比一项常规活动就是一种优势。”专家说，至少在一项课外活动中展现出才华，对大学录取有帮助，在顶尖本科院校尤其如此。“在某一类课外活动中脱颖而出，在录取过程中可以是加分项，对高度挑剔的院校尤其如此——在这些学校，成绩和考试分数拔尖已不足够，”常春藤智略（Ivy Wise）招生咨询公司的招生顾问凯蒂·凯利在邮件中写道。“学生需要具备那种品质或‘钩子’，能打动招生官，让他们能想象这个学生来到校园后会如何丰富校园社群。”
blocks.exp: 定位本块末引语：Distinguishing yourself in one focused type of extracurricular activity can be a positive ... especially for highly selective institutions——在某一类活动中出众会受顶尖院校青睐，故 A。D 的“经商能力”出自本块中的 Valdes，他不在 41–45 之列；本块前半的“个人项目”“非常规活动”也都是引子，别把整段的例子当成凯利的观点。

blocks.en: Extracurricular activities related to the college major declared on a college application are beneficial, experts suggest. “If you already know your major, having an extracurricular that fits into that major can be a big plus,” says Mayghin Levine, the manager of educational opportunities with The Cabbage Patch Settlement House, a Louisville, Kentucky, nonprofit community center.
blocks.zh: 专家建议，与申请表中填报的大学专业相关的课外活动是有益的。“如果你已经知道自己的专业，有一项与该专业契合的课外活动会是大加分项，”肯塔基州路易斯维尔非营利社区中心“卷心菜园安置屋”教育机会项目经理梅金·莱文说。
blocks.exp: 定位本块：having an extracurricular that fits into that major can be a big plus——选与未来专业相关的活动，与 G 的 related to their future study at college 同义，故 G。A 的“顶尖院校青睐”是上一块凯利的观点，方向相近但主体不同，是本题最易误配的一项。

blocks.en: High school students who have had a strong positive influence on their community through an extracurricular activity may impress a college and win a scholarship, says Erica Gwyn, a former math and science magnet program assistant at a public high school who is now executive director of the Kaleidoscope Careers Academy in Atlanta, a nonprofit organization.
blocks.zh: 亚特兰大非营利组织“万花筒职业发展学院”执行主任、曾任公立高中数学与科学特长项目助理的埃里卡·格温说，通过课外活动对社区产生了强烈积极影响的高中生，可能会给大学留下印象并获得奖学金。
blocks.exp: 定位末段：have had a strong positive influence on their community ... may impress a college and win a scholarship——惠及社区者更易获奖学金，与 B 的 has benefited their community 同义，故 B。C 的“活动过多不加分”是 Rexford 的观点，与本段的“社区影响”无关，属张冠李戴。

sections.title: Section III　翻译
sections.dir: In this section there is a text in English. Translate it into Chinese. Write your translation on ANSWER SHEET 2. (15 points)
sections.note: 按句给分：先切主谓。with 独立结构、which 定语从句、破折号插入语是三个难点。

paras.en: With the smell of coffee and fresh bread floating in the air, stalls bursting with colorful vegetables and tempting cheeses, and the buzz of friendly chats, farmers' markets are a feast for the senses. They also provide an opportunity to talk to the people responsible for growing or raising your food, support your local economy and pick up fresh seasonal produce — all at the same time.
paras.zh: 空气中飘着咖啡和新鲜面包的香味，摊位上堆满五颜六色的蔬菜和诱人的奶酪，还有友好交谈的嗡嗡声——农贸市场是一场感官的盛宴。它们还让人有机会与种植或养殖你食物的人交谈、支持本地经济，并买到新鲜的时令农产品——而这一切可以同时完成。

paras.en: Farmers' markets are usually weekly or monthly events, most often with outdoor stalls, which allow farmers or producers to sell their food directly to customers. The size or regularity of markets can vary from season to season, depending on the area's agricultural calendar, and you're likely to find different produce on sale at different times of the year. By cutting out the middlemen, the farmers secure more profit for their produce. Shoppers also benefit from seeing exactly where — and to who — their money is going.
paras.zh: 农贸市场通常每周或每月举办一次，多数设有露天摊位，让农民或生产者直接把食物卖给顾客。市场的规模或举办频率会随季节变化，取决于当地的农事日历，因此你在一年中不同的时候很可能买到不同的农产品。通过省去中间商，农民为自己的农产品争取到更多利润。购物者也能确切看到自己的钱去了哪里、流向了谁，这也是一种好处。

sections.title: Section IV Part A　应用文（事务邮件）
sections.dir: Suppose you and Jack are going to do a survey on the protection of old houses in an ancient town. Write him an email to 1) put forward your plan, and 2) ask for his opinion. Write your answer in about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET. Do not use your own name. Use “Li Ming” instead. (10 points)
sections.note: 两个任务点：①给出可执行的调查方案 ②明确征询 Jack 的意见。只写“我们加油”等于没写。
sections.sample:
Dear Jack,

I am writing to share my plan for our survey on the protection of old houses in the ancient town, and to hear what you think of it.

I suggest we focus on the two streets behind the old theatre, where more than thirty houses date back to the Qing dynasty. Two mornings there should be enough: first photographing each house and noting its condition, then interviewing residents and the local heritage office about repair costs and current rules. A short questionnaire for shop owners would add their views.

Does this sound workable to you? If you prefer, we can start with the temple area instead. Please let me know before Friday.

Yours,
Li Ming
tips: 第一段一句话点明写信目的：给出调查方案并征询意见，不要写成通知或说明书
方案要落地：调查对象（哪条街的老房子）、方法（拍照、访谈、问卷）、时间安排，三样至少写两样
第二段末尾必须明确问一句“你觉得可行吗”，否则“ask for his opinion”这一项不得分
语气是同学之间的商量，可用 Does this sound workable 一类说法；署名固定 Li Ming，不写真实姓名

sections.title: Section IV Part B　图表作文
sections.dir: Write an essay based on the chart below. In your writing, you should 1) describe and interpret the chart, and 2) give your comments. You should write about 150 words in the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
sections.note: 图表：某高校劳动实践课学生主要收获，知识 91.3%、动手 84.8% 居前，合作仅 32.6% 垫底。
sections.sample:
The bar chart shows what students gained from a labour practice course at a certain university. Knowledge comes first: 91.3 percent say they learned something relevant. Nearly as many, 84.8 percent, report improved hands-on skills, while 54.4 percent mention feeling cheerful, and only 32.6 percent cite stronger teamwork.

Two features stand out. The gap between knowing and doing is narrow, which suggests the course really does combine instruction with practice rather than leaving it at theory. Teamwork, by contrast, ranks last, most probably because tasks are assigned to individuals and assessed on personal output instead of on group results.

Such courses are valuable, but they could be better. If teachers designed more group projects and gave credit for cooperation, the weakest item on the chart would rise, and students would leave with skills they can use with others, not merely by themselves.
tips: 第一段只读数：91.3% 学知识、84.8% 练动手，两者接近，这是全图最有信息量的对比
第二段要解释“合作能力为何垫底”：任务多为个人完成、评分看个人成果，别泛泛说“学生不重视合作”
第三段给一条可操作的建议（增加小组任务、把合作纳入评分），正好呼应图表最低项
四个数据不必全报，54.4% 一笔带过即可；注意这是百分比，不要说成“增长了 91.3%”
